(4) FLOWS-lens-1's trigger population is narrower than the reviewer states: UserDefaults is included in an iCloud/iTunes backup, so ackedCloudIDs is NOT empty on a plain restore; the reachable population is pre-round-10 drops plus any drop whose cloud copy exists under a uid the current session's uid-scoped query cannot see. The DEFECT (a negative fact asserted from absence of evidence over a narrowed query) is structural and I confirm it on that ground, not on the reviewer's population estimate. (5) I flag a real cost of that fix which no reviewer priced: keying on `ownerUid != nil` will raise 'the cloud copy may still exist' for drops whose server copy was legitimately deleted externally, and under the live v2 rules that alarm CANNOT retire (retirement is capability-gated and the capability is .denied — verified). The fix is still correct per binding rule 1 (UNKNOWN is the honest answer), but it makes the v3 deploy a harder dependency, and the surface needs an acknowledge affordance. (6) I did not exhaustively audit ARScreen's state machine for every path that reaches the adjust panel on a received drop; I verified the panel has no ownership gate (ARScreen.swift:283-286) and that both commit paths call library.update(persist:) with no ownership check (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1645-1658, :1822-1831), which is sufficient for STATE-lens-1's trigger but not a complete AR audit.
research.shipVerdict: NOT production-grade for the Wave C charter. Round 10 genuinely closed most of what it claimed — ux-1, ux-2/flows-2, flows-3, seams-2, seams-6, seams-7, flows-5(partly), ux-7, seams-8, own-2(local half), ux-3, and the seams-1a deployed-rules pin are real, traced, and in two cases executed here. But four charter violations survive or were newly created, and two of them sit on the product's signature flow. BLOCKERS (must fix before ship): (B1) The receive flow's verdicts are INVERTED against the ruleset this very round pinned as live. I executed the proof: under web/firestore.rules.deployed a GET of an absent document DENIES. So a deleted or private drop throws, and the recipient is told 'Can't reach the server / You seem to be offline — the surprise may still be waiting' with an endless,永-failing Try again; meanwhile the authoritative 'The sender may have taken it back, or the link expired' is producible ONLY by client-side conditions (no plist, a decode failure). Round 10 built flows-6 on the assumption that nil means the server answered, and the same round committed the evidence that it does not. On a first-ever launch opened from a link (the recipient-installs-the-app moment) the same throw path also fires while anonymous sign-in is still in flight — AccountService.start() attaches synchronously only when a keychain user already exists (AccountService.swift:26-29). Fix: three-valued SharedDropFetch (.found/.absent/.unknown), permission-denied and unauthenticated and unconfigured all -> .unknown with retryable non-causal copy, and gate the initial load on uid != nil. (B2) redeem() cannot recall a delete already staged in Firestore's durable mutation queue (own-A). The feature's headline story — delete, then re-open your own link to get it back — restores the row locally and lets the queued delete destroy the cloud copy, killing every recipient's link with no surface anywhere. (B3) The evidence latch is wiped at the end of the only guaranteed post-auth refresh (RootView.swift:164 then :168; DropStore.swift:645). Three reviewers converged and I confirm: hasCompletedCleanRefresh is false for the whole session on the default Home/You path, so round 10's own ux-4 rung — the only surface for an outbox with no loadable rows — can never render, and the ladder is pinned at 'Checking sync status…'. Round 10 paired a new reset with a new gate and made a real failure LESS visible than round 9. One-line reorder plus a composed authDidBecomeReady() entry point. (B4) redeem()'s pending-edit guard is structurally empty for the exact category it serves — enqueueCloudSync returns at DropStore.swift:809 before markPending for every receivedViaLink row, so a received drop can never be in pendingSyncIDs, and re-opening a link silently destroys every AR placement adjustment the recipient made (persisted, no ownership gate at ARScreen.swift:283-286 / GeoARSessionManager.swift:1653, :1826); the mirror case discards the fetched copy entirely when a pending id has no row, which is precisely the post-quarantine state where the server copy is the last one left. STRONGLY RECOMMENDED IN THE SAME PASS: the non-additive phase-1 publish (DropStore.swift:481) — own-2 fixed the local strand and opened a cloud strand, blinking a restored library to 'No drops yet' on every refresh and stranding it there if any mutator lands during the cloud read, while churning the reaction listeners' primed watermark; and the two halves of the acked-evidence problem (fabricated positives from latency-compensated rows, false all-clears from absence of evidence), which are one root cause: ackedCloudIDs is doing per-object provenance work with set membership. WHAT IS ACTUALLY CLEAN: FirestoreAcked's four outcome mappings, the refusal taxonomy and its terminal-verdict plumbing, tombstone suppression in both publish phases, generation discipline in the save and delete pipelines, serverConfirmsAbsent's cache-proofness, the ReactionRecap model (it is the pattern the drop read should copy), the deployed-rules pin plus drift lock, and the ProfileScreen ladder's ORDER and per-rung copy. The mechanisms round 10 built are largely right; what fails is where they are WIRED (RootView's ordering, ReceiveScreen's mapping, redeem's guard predicate, phase-1's authority) — which is why the fix list is short, surgical, and worth one more round rather than a redesign.

verdicts.findingId: SEAMS-lens-1 (markAcked earned from latency-compensated rows)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified in source: FirebaseDropStore.swift:64-77 builds CloudRead from `snapshot.metadata.isFromCache` ONLY; CloudRead (DropStore.swift:50-53) has no per-row field; DropStore.swift:503 then :508 `if cloudReadServerServed { markAcked(drop.id) }` for every returned row, persisted durably to UserDefaults `ackedCloudDropIDs` (:397, :1006-1010). The platform contract: Firestore applies the local mutation queue to query results before delivering them (latency compensation) — a QuerySnapshot fetched from the backend reports `metadata.isFromCache == false` while individual DocumentSnapshots report `metadata.hasPendingWrites == true` for rows the server has not committed. Snapshot-level isFromCache answers 'did a server serve this READ'; it does not answer 'has the server committed THIS ROW'. So a staged-but-unacked create can mint the durable 'the server has seen this id' fact. The inconsistency is decisive evidence this is an oversight, not a trade: the same codebase already does per-document provenance twice — ReactionService.swift:183 filters `!$0.metadata.hasPendingWrites`, AccountService.swift:60-63 requires `!isFromCache && !hasPendingWrites` before retiring a status. The harm chain's terminal half is EXECUTED-verified here: retirement needs knownAbsenceCapability == .answers (DropStore.swift:593) and under the live ruleset probeAbsenceCapability returns .denied — I ran deployed-rules.test.mjs and 'absent-doc GET denies' passes — so a false unresolvedDelete can never clear before the v3 deploy. I confirm at HIGH but note the trigger requires a subsequent PERMANENT rejection of the staged write (a rejected mutation is rolled out of the queue, but the durable acked fact already written survives), which is narrower than the reviewer's prose implies.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Carry provenance per row, exactly as the Firestore idiom prescribes. Add `var serverConfirmedIDs: Set<UUID>` to CloudRead (DropStore.swift:50-53). In FirebaseDropStore.loadDropsWithProvenance (:67-77) build it inside the existing compactMap: `if !document.metadata.hasPendingWrites { confirmed.insert(cloud.drop.id) }` — every row still merges for display, only the evidence narrows. Change DropStore.swift:508 to `if cloudReadServerServed, read.serverConfirmedIDs.contains(drop.id) { markAcked(drop.id) }`. Per binding rule 6 the double must express the case: give GatedCloudStore `setUnackedRows(_: Set<UUID>)` and have loadDropsWithProvenance omit those ids from serverConfirmedIDs. Test testStagedRowInAServerServedReadEarnsNoAckedFact as the reviewer specifies — and note their vacuity call is right: it is UNWRITEABLE against today's double, so the double change is part of the fix, not a follow-up.

verdicts.findingId: SEAMS-lens-2 (no refusal taxonomy in the delete pipeline)
verdicts.reasoning: The MECHANISM is real: performCloudDelete's catch-all (DropStore.swift:924-948) spends an attempt on every thrown error with no call to DropStoreError.terminalRefusalReason, while the save path classifies at FirebaseDropStore.swift:131-133; FirebaseDropStore.delete (:147-172) rethrows raw. Also true and worth fixing: unresolvedDeleteIDs is never retried (reconcileCloud replays only pendingDeleteIDs, DropStore.swift:794-797) and the never-acked resolution at :945-947 leaves nothing but a log line. But the HEADLINE HARM is refuted by the platform contract. Firestore's write completion handler fires only when a mutation is committed by the backend or definitively rejected with a PERMANENT write error; the SDK classifies CANCELLED, UNKNOWN, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, INTERNAL, UNAVAILABLE and UNAUTHENTICATED as retryable and retries them internally on the write stream without invoking the callback (isPermanentWriteError = isPermanentError && code != ABORTED). So the reviewer's trigger — 'the project hits its Spark daily write quota (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) and three refreshes burn the budget' — cannot occur: those codes never reach DropStore.swift:924. Slowness is already absorbed correctly by FirestoreAcked's deadline -> .queuedLocally -> ackTimedOut -> no attempt spent (:921-923). Every code that DOES surface (INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_DENIED, FAILED_PRECONDITION, ALREADY_EXISTS, OUT_OF_RANGE, UNIMPLEMENTED, DATA_LOSS) is genuinely non-retryable, so spending an attempt on it is defensible. Severity accordingly drops from HIGH to LOW-MEDIUM: this is defense-in-depth and consistency, not a live data-loss path. Note also the reviewer has the budget backwards in one respect — deleteAttempts is in-memory (:381), so each LAUNCH grants a fresh 3 attempts, which is more forgiving, not less; the real durability defect is the one-way door into unresolvedDeleteIDs.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Three changes, cheap and independent. (1) Guard the attempt: in performCloudDelete before :937, `guard DropStoreError.terminalRefusalReason(error) != nil else { return }` — a transient code that somehow does surface leaves the tombstone pending for reconcileCloud instead of consuming the bound. (2) Make the bound a lifetime bound: persist deleteAttempts alongside pendingDeleteIDs (a `[String: Int]` defaults dictionary) so three refusals mean three, not three-per-launch. (3) Give unresolvedDeleteIDs a retry path — after the v3 deploy an absent-doc delete succeeds (verified: rules.test.mjs passes the absent-delete case), so reconcileCloud should replay unresolved ids once per session at low priority, and the never-acked DONE branch at :945-947 must leave an observable record (a durable resolvedWithoutProof set) rather than a log line. The reviewer's proposed test is sound but must use a code that actually reaches the callback to be honest — pin the ACTUAL classification against RefusalTaxonomyTests rather than inventing a transient-delete scenario the SDK cannot produce.

verdicts.findingId: SEAMS-lens-3 (cache-served read clears a server-issued sync error)
verdicts.reasoning: Exactly as traced. DropStore.swift:503 computes cloudReadServerServed and spends it on the latch (:569) and markAcked (:508), but :514 `lastSyncError = nil` is unconditional inside the do-block. The platform contract makes the cache-served success reachable without a throw: `getDocuments()` with the default source attempts the server and falls back to cached results when it is unreachable — it returns a QuerySnapshot with isFromCache == true rather than throwing (only single-document `getDocument()` with no cached copy throws the offline error). Meanwhile lastSyncError is set at :519 by a real server-answered failure — permission-denied under App Check enforcement, unauthenticated after a revoked token, or a failed-precondition/missing-index after the v3 deploy changes the query shape. So the sequence 'server refuses -> user goes offline -> cached read succeeds -> verdict silently revoked' is fully reachable, and it violates binding rule 4 (a verdict revoked by something that is neither its issuing authority nor the disappearance of its producing condition) and rule 3 (confirming state keyed on a read the SDK satisfied locally). Consumers ProfileScreen.swift:127 and DropsListScreen.swift:48 both go quiet; if evidence had already latched, the ladder falls through to 'Synced'. This is a one-line asymmetry left behind by the ux-1 work — the provenance flag exists eleven lines above and is simply not consulted here.
verdicts.industrialSolution: `if cloudReadServerServed { lastSyncError = nil }` at DropStore.swift:514. A cache-served read is not an authority and leaves the prior server verdict standing. Add the paired regression lock the reviewer describes (server-answered failure sets it; a subsequent cache-served success must NOT clear it, and hasCompletedCleanRefresh must stay false) — the second half already passes thanks to ux-1, which is what makes the pair a sharp lock on the remaining asymmetry rather than a vacuous restatement.

verdicts.findingId: SEAMS-lens-4 (fetchSharedDrop's nil is three different facts)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified line by line: DropSharingService.swift:53 returns nil when AppConfig.firebaseConfigured is false (a supported no-plist mode, AppConfig.swift:13-14), :57 returns nil for the honest !exists, :71 returns nil when the document EXISTS but the envelope decode throws — and the inner payload is still a hard decode (`drop = try c.decode(GeoDrop.self, forKey: .drop)` at :67), so the round-10 leniency covers ownerUid only. ReceiveScreen.swift:147-151 maps all three to .gone and renders the causal, non-retryable 'The sender may have taken it back, or the link expired' (:114-123, Try again gated to .unreachable at :124). This is a textbook binding-rule-1 violation: two of the three producers are fallthroughs that must resolve to UNKNOWN. The reviewer's hijack-driven decode trigger is real and I verified its premise by execution — deployed-rules.test.mjs's 'v2 DEFECT still present: stranger can hijack via update stamping own uid' passes, so any signed-in user can overwrite a drop document and turn every recipient's link into a permanent fabricated expiry. This finding is one half of the same defect as SURF-lens-2 (which owns the inverse direction: server answers that are thrown and rendered as offline). Fix them together or the copy stays wrong in one direction.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Replace the Optional with a total function over the three real outcomes: `enum SharedDropFetch { case found(GeoDrop); case absent; case unknown(reason: String) }`. ONLY `snapshot.exists == false` yields .absent. The unconfigured guard, the envelope/payload decode failure, and every thrown error (mapping FirestoreErrorCode.permissionDenied and .unauthenticated explicitly) yield .unknown. Make the inner payload decode lenient too, or at minimum route its failure to .unknown rather than .absent. ReceiveScreen renders .unknown with retryable, non-causal copy and reserves the expiry claim for .absent — which, note, becomes producible only after the v3 deploy (firestore.rules:52-55 tolerates resource == null), so until then the honest product behaviour is 'this link can't be opened right now' plus retry, never an expiry verdict. The reviewer's test is right and fills a genuine void: no test in AugmentMeRealityTests references DropSharingService or ReceiveScreen at all.

verdicts.findingId: SEAMS-lens-5 (drift lock covers only the emoji list)
verdicts.reasoning: Factually correct and I verified it: drift-check.mjs parses exactly two things (ReactionSession.reactions at :13-19 and the `data.emoji in [...]` list at :21-28); the `keys().hasOnly(['id','emoji','uid','byName','at'])` clause at firestore.rules:78 is asserted only by rules.test.mjs against a hardcoded payload, and the true contract is DropReaction's synthesized encoding (ReactionService.swift:10-16). Nothing connects the three lists. But there is NO CURRENT DEFECT: DropReaction encodes exactly id, emoji, uid, byName, at — the sets match today, and I executed the suite ('reaction with extra keys denied' passes). So this is a regression-prevention gap, not a live harm, and D2 requires me to price it as such: severity LOW, not HIGH. The reviewer's framing of WHEN it would bite is the valuable part and is correct — v2 has no key restriction (firestore.rules.deployed:39-40), so a drift would be invisible in production and detonate at the moment of the v3 deploy. That makes it a release-gate item alongside the Wave A deploy, not a shipping blocker.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Extend drift-check.mjs with a `reactionKeys()` pair mirroring the emoji pair: parse the stored property names from `struct DropReaction` in ReactionService.swift (regex over the `var <name>:` lines between the struct braces) and the `keys().hasOnly([...])` literal from firestore.rules, and exit non-zero on any set difference; then have rules.test.mjs build its reaction payload from the parsed list exactly as it already does via appEmojiList() rather than the literal at :96-98. Because npm test runs drift-check first (package.json:7), the failure lands before the emulator starts. Bind this to the Wave A deploy checklist so it cannot be deferred past the rules cutover.

verdicts.findingId: SEAMS-lens-6 (absence-capability latch is never re-armed)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified: DropStore.swift:586-592 probes only when knownAbsenceCapability == nil and latches any non-.inconclusive answer for the life of the DropLibrary (one per process, constructed at AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:18); accountDidChange() (:642-651) resets hasCompletedCleanRefresh but not the capability; FirebaseDropStore.probeAbsenceCapability (:204-209) maps ANY FirestoreErrorCode.permissionDenied to .denied, which cannot distinguish 'the rules cannot answer absence' from 'App Check rejected this client' or 'this token is revoked'. The reviewer's own counter-analysis is correct and I confirm it: the probe itself is sound and unfabricable (a random UUID cannot exist; I executed both suites and v2 denies the absent get while v3 answers it). Severity is LOW and should be sequenced with the v3 deploy, because under the CURRENTLY DEPLOYED rules the latch is .denied by design — every retirement probe is skipped in production today regardless of this defect. The finding becomes live the moment v3 ships, and trigger B (a long-lived session that latched .denied before the deploy never re-probes) is a real deploy-day consideration.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Give .denied a bounded life and a sharper cause. (1) Reset knownAbsenceCapability in accountDidChange() alongside hasCompletedCleanRefresh — a new account connection is a new rules subject. (2) Re-probe a latched .denied after N refreshes or on scenePhase .active, so a mid-session v3 deploy is picked up without a relaunch; .answers may stay latched (capability does not regress silently). (3) Before concluding .denied, probe a path the rules always permit for the signed-in user — `users/{uid}` get, which BOTH rulesets allow and which the suite already asserts (rules.test.mjs 'own ABSENT user doc answers') — and map a denial there to .inconclusive, since it indicates App Check/token trouble rather than absent-doc semantics. verdicts.findingId: STATE-lens-3 (RootView destroys the evidence latch the auth-ready refresh just earned)

"-")` awaits library.refresh(near: nil) at :164 — the only place hasCompletedCleanRefresh is set (DropStore.swift:569-571) — then calls library.accountDidChange() at :168, whose first statement is `hasCompletedCleanRefresh = false` (:645, new in round 10). verdicts.findingId: STATE-lens-4 (two-phase publish destroys the published cloud half)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified, and I raise the severity to HIGH. DropStore.swift:449-481: `merged` is populated ONLY from the local load at :452-454; the cloud read happens afterwards at :487-513; so `var localOnly = merged` at :478 followed by `drops = localOnly.values.sorted…` at :481 unconditionally REPLACES the published set with a local-only set. Seed from what is already published before overlaying the fresh local load: `var localOnly = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: drops.map { ($0.id, $0) })`, then overlay the loaded local rows, then apply both tombstone sets, then publish. A row the previous completed refresh contributed is never dropped by a partial pass, and phase 2 remains the authoritative replace. Better still, and it fixes the root: persist server-served cloud rows to the local store on merge (`try? await local.save(drop)` for rows in serverConfirmedIDs, reusing the SEAMS-lens-1 provenance), so local truth becomes a superset and phase 1 is genuinely complete — this also stops the reaction-listener churn described in FLOWS-lens-4 at its source. Test: with a parked cloud load, assert library.drops is never observed empty, and after a mutator supersedes the pass assert both the cloud row and the new row are present. Existing testDeleteDuringRefreshIsNotResurrectedByThePublish (DropStoreTests.swift:338-358) checks only tombstone suppression and passes with or without the phase-1 publish.

verdicts.findingId: STATE-lens-5 (prefix(5) over an unordered Set starves the tombstone tail)

verdicts.findingId: STATE-lens-6 (remove() commits a multi-step transition across an await without re-validating)

verdicts.findingId: SURF-lens-2 (gone-vs-unreachable inverted against the deployed rules)
verdicts.reasoning: The single most important finding of the round, and I verified its load-bearing premise BY EXECUTION rather than by argument. I ran both emulator suites: web/rules-tests/deployed-rules.test.mjs asserts 'absent-doc GET denies (capability probe must report .denied)' against web/firestore.rules.deployed and it PASSES — the v2 read rule (firestore.rules.deployed:30-32) dereferences resource.data on a null resource, which in the Firestore rules language is an evaluation error and therefore a denial. So under the ruleset this very round pinned as live, a deleted or private drop answers PERMISSION_DENIED, i.e. the THROW branch — ReceiveScreen.swift:152-153 renders it as 'Can't reach the server / You seem to be offline — the surprise may still be waiting' with a Try again (:124-128) that can never succeed, while the honest .gone copy (:114-121) is producible only by client-side conditions (no plist at DropSharingService.swift:53, a decode failure at :71). verdicts.industrialSolution: One change closes this and SEAMS-lens-4 together. (1) fetchSharedDrop returns `SharedDropFetch { case found(GeoDrop); case absent; case unknown(reason) }` — .absent ONLY from `snapshot.exists == false`; permission-denied, unauthenticated, unconfigured, and any decode failure all map to .unknown. (2) ReceiveScreen renders .unknown with copy that asserts no cause and offers retry ('This link can't be opened right now — it may have been taken back, or your account is still connecting'), and reserves 'taken back / the link expired' for .absent, which only becomes producible after the v3 deploy (firestore.rules:52-55 tolerates resource == null — verified passing in rules.test.mjs). (3) Gate the initial load on `account.uid != nil`, or re-run load() when the uid arrives, so a healthy link never shows a failure screen during sign-in. Test the pure mapper (permissionDenied/unauthenticated -> .unknown; !exists -> .absent; unconfigured -> .unknown) plus a ReceiveScreen assertion that .unknown renders Try again — no test currently touches either file, and the emulator suite asserts the DENIAL only, saying nothing about how the client renders it, which is why the suite is green while the copy is inverted.

verdicts.findingId: SURF-lens-3 (Memory recap asserts an offline cause and promises a landing place)
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves verified. ReactionService.swift:186-192 returns serverAnswered == false for a cache-served snapshot AND for every thrown error (`return .unavailable` at :191 is byte-identical to the offline value), so a permission denial, an unauthenticated read, or a missing index all render through MemoryScreen.swift:74-81's single branch as 'Reactions land here when you're back online' — a fabricated cause. The promise is unbacked: the recap is read exactly once (`.task { recap = await reactions.reactions(for: drop) }`, MemoryScreen.swift:102) with no retry and no connectivity observer; the screen is a fullScreenCover whose dismissal calls endSession() (RootView.swift:78-81) which nils the drop, and there is no Memory history anywhere (ProfileScreen.swift:170 says captures 'appear here from Wave 6.2'). Note this is a correctness gap in an area that is otherwise the best code in the round — the recap's provenance model (per-document hasPendingWrites, own-uid exclusion, snapshot-level serverAnswered, errors to UNKNOWN rather than an empty list) is the pattern the drop read should copy. The defect is the collapse of two distinct unknowns into one, and copy that outruns the mechanism.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Split the unknown at the source and stop promising what nothing delivers. Give ReactionRecap a reason (`enum RecapState { case answered; case cached; case failed(Error) }` replacing the bare Bool), render .cached as a state without a promise ('Reactions aren't loaded yet') and .failed as its own line, never as an offline claim. Then either BACK the promise — re-run reactions(for:) from a retry affordance and on a connectivity/uid change keyed `.task` — or reword it to what the mechanics support. Test over a pure copy function fed both inputs and assert the two strings differ and that neither promises a future arrival unless a re-read path exists; ReactionSessionTests covers only the own-line delivery pill and never constructs a recap, so it passes with and without this defect.

verdicts.findingId: SURF-lens-4 (listener pruning kills the sender's toast for drops leaving the newest-10 window)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified: ReactionService.swift:116-121 computes the detach set from `mine`, which is Self.watchedDrops(...) capped at `prefix(10)` (:81-89), so an 11th owned non-private drop pushes the oldest out of the DISPLAY cap and now also tears down its listener AND drops its primed watermark. RootView.swift:155-157 re-runs the pass on every listenKey change and the key is exactly the watched-set identity (:97-102), so the pruning executes the moment the 11th drop exists. Before round 10 the dictionary only grew, so a listener attached for a drop that later left the newest-10 kept delivering — this is a strict behavioural regression introduced by flows-5, and the toast (RootView.swift:101-126) is the only sender-side reaction surface, since the profile counters are written by nothing (ProfileScreen.swift:55-66) — the deferred ux-5 residual. So round 10 made a recorded residual materially more dangerous, which D5 designates a finding. Severity MEDIUM: the reaction that reads as ignored is the most damaging false state this product can produce.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Separate the LISTEN set from the DISPLAY cap. Compute the detach set against the full eligible library (`drops.filter { owned && !private && !receivedViaLink }`) so only drops that genuinely left the library (deleted, foreign, received) release their registration, and compute the attach set against a much larger bound — Firestore's documented ceiling is 100 concurrent snapshot listeners per client, so 50 is safe and 10 was never a platform constraint. Keep primedListeners keyed by drop id BEYOND the registration's lifetime so a re-attach cannot re-prime and swallow a reaction. Test over an extracted pure `listenerPlan(currentKeys:library:myUid:) -> (attach:[String], detach:[String])`: a drop displaced only by the cap must not appear in detach; a deleted or received drop must. ReactionListenKeyTests.swift:62 asserts the cap itself and passes whether or not existing listeners are torn down.

verdicts.findingId: SURF-lens-5 (skipped-rows Dismiss is a guaranteed no-op; 'sync is on hold' is false)
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves verified, and the round-10 interaction is exactly as claimed. LocalDropStore.loadDrops re-derives the incident on EVERY load of the same file — DropStore.swift:202-212 writes pendingReadWarning and calls writeIncident whenever any row fails to decode, and the bad rows STAY on disk (only the whole-file path moves the file, :227-232). acknowledgeReadIncident (:620-636) clears the journal and then, because of round 10's ux-3 change, immediately awaits refresh(near: nil) at :634 — which reloads the same bytes, re-journals, and re-publishes localReadWarning at :466-468. verdicts.findingId: FLOWS-lens-1 (bounded-refusal delete resolves DONE from absence of evidence)
verdicts.reasoning: I confirm the structural defect and correct the severity and the population. STRUCTURE (decisive): DropStore.swift:943 asserts the NEGATIVE fact 'the server never held this id' from `!ackedCloudIDs.contains(id)` — absence of evidence — and that set is fed in part by a uid-scoped query (FirebaseDropStore.swift:64-66), so it is precisely the set-difference-over-a-narrowed-query that binding rule 2 forbids, with the good state ('nothing to warn about') reached by fallthrough, which rule 1 forbids. remove() destroys the distinguishing evidence first: :742 local.delete erases the row and its ownerUid from disk, :753 clearTerminal discards the ownedByAnotherAccount verdict, and performCloudDelete's ghost (:911-912) carries only the id, so FirebaseDropStore.delete's owner backstop (:153) cannot fire. Under v2 a delete denies identically for an absent doc and for a foreign-owned doc — I executed the absent case ('absent-doc DELETE denies' passes) and the owner clause at firestore.rules.deployed:35-36 gives the other, so the error alone cannot separate them. The fix premise is sound: I grepped every writer of ownerUid and it is set ONLY from server-sourced values (FirebaseDropStore.swift:100 stamps before the write but the stamped copy is returned only on `.acked` at :121-122, DropStore.swift:850-856 persists it only after that ack; FirebaseDropStore.swift:72-73 and DropSharingService.swift:72-73 from server reads), so `ownerUid != nil` on a local row is a true positive per-object check. CORRECTIONS: the transient-rejection half is refuted (see SEAMS-lens-2 — the SDK never surfaces retryable write codes to the completion), and 'empty for every restored install' is wrong (UserDefaults is included in device backups, so ackedCloudIDs restores with the library). The genuinely reachable population is pre-round-10 drops whose cloud copy is owned by a previous uid, which the uid-scoped read can never re-ack. Severity HIGH rather than CRITICAL.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Capture the positive fact at tombstone time, while it still exists. In remove(), BEFORE clearTerminal at :753, record into a durable set (`cloudProvenIDs`, defaults key cloudProvenDropIDs): `drop.ownerUid != nil || ackedCloudIDs.contains(drop.id) || terminalSyncFailureIDs.contains(drop.id)`. performCloudDelete:943 then keys on that set: proven -> markUnresolvedDelete (visible UNKNOWN); not proven -> DONE. PRICE THIS EXPLICITLY, because no reviewer did: keying on ownerUid also raises the alarm for drops whose server copy was legitimately removed out of band, and under the live v2 rules that alarm CANNOT retire (retirement is capability-gated and the capability is .denied — verified by execution). That is the correct answer per binding rule 1 (UNKNOWN is honest) but it makes the Wave A v3 deploy a harder dependency and the ProfileScreen unresolved-delete rung needs an acknowledge affordance so the user is not stuck with a permanent unknown. Test as the reviewer specifies (a local drop with ownerUid = 'old-uid' and an EMPTY ackedCloudDropIDs, three refused deletes, assert unresolvedDeleteIDs contains the id); testNeverAckedDeleteResolvesWithoutCloudCopyAlarm (DropStoreTests.swift:858-881) uses a drop with ownerUid nil and passes with and without the fix.

verdicts.findingId: FLOWS-lens-2 (redeem discards the received drop when the pending id has no live row)
verdicts.reasoning: Duplicate in substance of STATE-lens-2 — same call site, same predicate, same fix — and I confirm it once. This lens contributes the sharper end-to-end trigger, which I verified: pendingSyncIDs hydrates from defaults at DropStore.swift:415-416 independently of any disk row; a whole-file quarantine MOVES the store file (LocalDropStore.swift:227-241) so subsequent loads report .quarantinedWholeFile then .absentFile; the reap is gated on `if case .clean` (DropStore.swift:536) so the orphaned pending id survives every launch. In that state the user opens a magic link, ReceiveScreen fetches successfully, RootView.swift:66 calls redeem, the guard at :679 fires, nothing is inserted and nothing is written, redeem does not throw so RootView's catch (:67-71) never fires, and RootView.swift:73-74 starts the AR session on an in-memory-only value. The one recoverable copy of the drop is refused precisely when it is the only one left.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Same single corrected predicate as STATE-lens-1/STATE-lens-2: insert + local.save when no local row exists; keep the local row (no write) when one does. Optionally return a typed outcome so RootView can tell 'stored' from 'kept your copy'. The reviewer's test (defaults seeded with pendingSyncDropIDs = [id] over a LocalDropStore pointed at a non-existent file, then redeem, then assert the row is in `drops` AND on disk) is the right lock and is non-vacuous — testRedeemNeverOverwritesAPendingLocalEdit adds the drop first, so the row always exists and the early return is correct behaviour there.

verdicts.findingId: FLOWS-lens-3 (auth-ready task wipes the evidence; ux-4 rung unreachable)
verdicts.reasoning: Third independent confirmation of the same defect (see STATE-lens-3 and SURF-lens-1); the trace is correct in every particular and I verified the claim that nothing re-refreshes automatically (AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:34 pre-auth only, no refresh in the scenePhase .active branch at :35-51, MapScreen.swift:105-107 Explore-only, DropsListScreen.swift:25-26 manual). This lens adds the correct causal attribution: round 10's lens-4 change CREATED the suppression — before it the latch survived the refresh — and it was paired in the same round with a new failure surface gated behind that latch, which is the D5 pattern exactly. AccountService.swift:25-40 confirms uid transitions nil -> uid once per launch for anonymous sign-in (with the warm-launch path attaching synchronously at :26-29), so this is not an edge case: it is every launch.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Identical to STATE-lens-3: move the ordering inside DropLibrary as authDidBecomeReady(uid:) — reset conditionally on an actual uid change, then await refresh — so no call site can re-break it, and add a scenePhase-active refresh. Regression lock as specified: assert (hasCompletedCleanRefresh && unpushablePendingCount == 1) after the composed pass with a seeded orphan pending id, which is the surface production actually suppresses; testAccountChangeResetsSyncEvidence asserts only the reset half of the contract.

verdicts.findingId: FLOWS-lens-4 (phase-1 publish churns AR entities and the reaction watermark)
verdicts.reasoning: Same root as STATE-lens-4 (non-additive phase 1) and I confirm both; this lens contributes the consequence that makes it more than a UI flash, and the chain holds. `await provenanced.loadDropsWithProvenance(...)` at DropStore.swift:491 yields the main actor between the phase-1 publish (:481) and the phase-2 publish (:527), so SwiftUI renders in between. RootView.swift:155-157 keys the reaction listeners on ReactionService.listenKey(for: library.drops, ...), which is a pure function of the watched drop-ID set (ReactionService.swift:97-102) — so the reduced set changes the key, the task re-runs, and round 10's pruning at :116-121 removes the registration AND `primedListeners.remove(key)`. Phase 2 restores the key, the listener re-attaches un-primed, and its initial snapshot — `.order(by:"at", descending:true).limit(to:1)` at :128 — is swallowed as history at :145-148. So a reaction landing in the detach window is discarded permanently. For any install whose rows are cloud-only (restore, second device, post-quarantine) this happens on EVERY refresh. The AR half is equally real: GeoARSessionManager recomputes from library.drops each tick and tears down holders, content entities, groundLockBaseY and deferred VPS transforms for ids that vanish. Round 10 attached listener pruning to an array that own-2 made churn — a recorded residual (the seams-5 watermark) made strictly more fragile, which D5 designates a finding.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Fix the root (additive phase 1, or persist server-confirmed cloud rows locally so local truth is a superset — see STATE-lens-4) and independently decouple listener lifetime from a transient publish: keep primedListeners keyed by drop id across the registration's lifetime so a re-attach never re-primes, and prune a listener only after its drop has been absent from the watched set across a COMPLETED refresh rather than on any published snapshot. Test: with the cloud load parked, assert library.drops is never observed without the cloud-only row, and assert the listener plan produces no detach for a row that is merely mid-refresh.

verdicts.findingId: FLOWS-lens-5 (failed incident-journal write is indistinguishable from no incident)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified and correct in every step. LocalDropStore.writeIncident swallows its result (`try? ... write(to: incidentNoteURL, options: .atomic)` at DropStore.swift:276-278) — round 10's lens-6 work checked the moveItem result at :232 and the sidecar at :261-274 but left the load-bearing artifact unchecked. On a whole-file corruption the quarantine sets pendingReadWarning = nil (:234) and journals (:238-240); if that write fails, lastLoadReadWarning() (:286-292) returns nil, and once the file has been moved the next load returns `.absentFile` with a nil warning (:180-187), so `case .absentFile?: return localReadWarning == nil` at :565 evaluates TRUE and the latch is set at :570 — 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' over an emptied library. The disk-full correlation argument is sound: the condition most likely to truncate a JSON write is the one most likely to fail the journal write. testQuarantineAbsenceEarnsNoPositiveEvidence (DropStoreTests.swift:680-699) runs in a writable tmp dir where the journal always succeeds and therefore cannot catch it. I confirm, and I extend it: the same clause is reachable with NO failure at all, through the normal Dismiss affordance that round 10 made the ONLY retirement path — see my own finding own-B, which subsumes this one and shares its fix.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Fix the clause, not just the swallowed error. Primary: make `.absentFile` earn cleanliness only when no quarantine artifact exists beside the store — check for `drops.json.corrupt-*` and `drops.json.unreadable-*` on load and downgrade the outcome if any is present. That is durable, non-dismissable, filesystem-resident evidence, it survives a failed journal write, and it also covers a failed moveItem (in which case the original file is still present and the outcome is not `.absentFile` anyway). Secondary, as the reviewer says: make writeIncident return Bool and latch a `journalWriteFailed` flag that forces lastLoadOutcome()/lastLoadReadWarning() to report non-clean for the rest of the process. Test with a read-only directory (or an injected journal-write failure seam): after quarantine + absent-file refreshes, assert !hasCompletedCleanRefresh and localReadWarning != nil.

verdicts.findingId: FLOWS-lens-6 (flows-5 releases the dead listener but nothing re-attaches it)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified and correct on the platform contract, which is what makes it a real finding rather than a style note. ReactionService.swift:132-144 removes the registration and clears primedListeners so 'the next listen pass re-attaches', but the only caller is RootView.swift:155-157's `.task(id: ReactionService.listenKey(...))`, and listenKey (:97-102) is a function of the watched drop-ID set alone — an unchanged set yields an unchanged id and SwiftUI never re-runs the body, so there is no next pass. The platform half: a Firestore snapshot listener's error callback is TERMINAL — the SDK retries transient failures internally without invoking the callback and serves from cache, so the callback fires only when the listen has been given up (permission-denied after a rules change, an unrecoverable auth failure, a resource-exhausted listen). That is exactly the case that needs an explicit re-attach, and the code has none. Net behaviour is identical to pre-round-10 (dead for the session) with a comment that now claims otherwise — a claim the mechanics cannot back, which is the charter's own wording. One caveat on the reviewer's harm framing: FLOWS-lens-4's churn does incidentally re-attach in the cloud-only-rows case, so 'dead for the session' is strictly true only for libraries whose watched set is stable — which is the normal case.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Give the release a trigger the view layer does not own. Track released keys inside ReactionService and schedule a bounded-backoff re-attach (Task + attempt counter, capped), and additionally call listenToMySharedDrops from the scenePhase == .active branch in AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:35-51 so a foreground return always repairs the set. Keep the primed watermark per drop id ACROSS the re-attach so the repair does not swallow a reaction that landed while detached (this is the same requirement FLOWS-lens-4 needs — one change serves both). Test behind an injectable attach seam counting attaches per key: drive the error callback and assert the count reaches 2 within the retry budget WITHOUT calling listenToMySharedDrops again — as the reviewer correctly notes, calling it would make the test vacuous. No existing test covers the listener lifecycle; ReactionListenKeyTests exercises only the pure key functions.
